latest_wiki.summary: The statue of Maimonides in Córdoba was vandalized with a swastika, according to the text.

About 17,500 antisemitic tweets were posted by Spanish users after Maccabi Tel Aviv won the EuroLeague on 18 May 2014. Twelve Jewish associations filed a judicial complaint over references to death camps and the Holocaust.
Real Madrid supporters made Nazi salutes and chanted 'Jew that I see, Jew that I hit' before a match against Inter Milano, according to the text. The text does not name the match location.
German planes dropped leaflets in the area offering a 50,000 Reichsmark reward for help in capturing Tuvia Bielski, later doubled to 100,000 RM. The leaflets were aimed at the Christian population.
The text reports that the Bielsko Synagogue was destroyed by Nazis on 13 September 1939. No further details are given.
After partisans revolted in Eupatoria, reprisals directed by Major Hans-Wolf Riesen of the Eleventh Army staff led to the execution of 1,200 civilians. The text says the bulk of them were Jews.
On 31 December 1958 the President of the Executive Council of Tripolitania ordered the dissolution of the Jewish Community Council and the appointment of a Muslim commissioner.
In 1947, rioters killed at least 80 Jews in Aden.
In 1934, pogroms took place in Thrace.
In 1948, 127 defenders and residents of Kfar Etzion were killed in a massacre during the siege by the Arab Legion and irregulars.
The text reports violent anti-Jewish violence in Cairo in 1945, resulting in 10 Jewish victims.
In 1967, after the Six-Day War, antisemitic riots broke out in Damascus.

latest_jta.summary: According to local press reports, a worker named Matrosov shut a Jewish co-worker in the steam department of a Moscow timber plant and turned on the steam. The Jewish worker was found unconscious, and Matrosov was arrested.
The article refers to an anti-Semitic fire in Borscha that burned Jewish homes. The Romanian cabinet granted aid to the Jews of Borscha and allowed use of timber for rebuilding.

Jewish religious heads protested that during King Carol's visits to Cluj, their delegation was given scattered seats in inconspicuous places, preventing it from addressing the King as a body. They attributed this to a Ministerial Director.

Unknown persons, believed to be members of the National-Democratic party, raided the offices of the Nasz Prezegland, a Polish-Jewish daily in Warsaw, and broke its windows. Police arrived and the raiders left.
Eight gravestones were smashed in a Jewish cemetery in Tilsit, East Prussia. The vandals were not caught. The article describes this as the 95th desecration of a Jewish cemetery in Germany.
The article reports that anti-Semitic demonstrators attacked Jewish passersby in Jassy near a Liberal political meeting before police dispersed them.

Five Jewish students at the University of Budapest were found with injuries from assaults the previous day. The article reports that anti-Jewish attacks on students had been occurring for several days.
A band of 25 anti-Semites entered the courtyards of the University of Budapest and tried to drive Jewish students from the school premises. Several Jews were injured.
Hitlerites attacked Jews on the streets of Danzig, beating them with blackjacks. Samuel Rosan and Isaak Roslin were taken to hospital in critical condition.
Hitlerites attacked Jews at the Cafe Corso in Zoppot, a suburb of Danzig, the previous day.

Two Jewish doctors, brothers, said a Westchester County Park Commission patrolman beat them after arresting them for smoking in a park swimming pool, and the court upheld the assault charges against him. The doctors had claimed in court that the assault was due to anti-Semitic feeling.
A gang of Hitlerites attacked Selig Preuss, a Jewish merchant, and his son, badly injuring both of them in Ortelsburg, East Prussia.

The article reports that a gang of Cuzists attacked Jewish passengers on a train from Novosielicz to Czernowitz, throwing their baggage off and pushing the Jews from the train. Hirsch Rosenblatt and Moses Lichtig, both of Czernowitz, were among those more seriously injured.
The article reports that eight Zionist students distributing campaign leaflets on the University of Vienna campus were attacked and injured by anti-Semitic students.

latest_research.summary: The Observatory on Antisemitism in Belgium reports that a paving stone was thrown through a third-floor window of the Orthodox Jewish community synagogue in Anderlecht, shattering the glass. The Observatory describes it as vandalism targeting a Jewish place of worship, and the US ambassador calls it an antisemitic attack. The perpetrator is unidentified.

Jewish News reports that a woman was filmed describing Jewish people as "killers and psychopaths" during a protest outside Sheffield Town Hall. South Yorkshire Police first recorded a hate incident. A later Jewish News report says police concluded the remarks did not amount to a recordable crime, and the lower, no-crime finding is the one noted here.

Two unknown persons threw Molotov cocktails at the Kahal Adass Jisroel synagogue complex on Brunnenstraße in Berlin-Mitte in the early morning. According to reports the devices landed on the pavement and no one was hurt.

A 26-year-old Jewish student wearing a kippah was struck on the head with a folding spade outside the Hohe Weide synagogue, according to the sources. Police assumed an antisemitic motive, and a later court ruling is reported to have found a targeted attack on a Jew.

Unknown persons scratched swastikas into several gravestones at the Jewish cemetery on Krankenhausstraße in Cloppenburg, and state security police investigated for incitement to hatred. Police later reported that two teenagers admitted the act.
Witnesses told police that a group of about 15 people gathered in front of the synagogue, shouted and burned an Israeli flag. State security police took over the investigation.

Police reported that a 24-year-old Jewish man was assaulted on a tram in Erfurt after another man noticed his Star of David necklace. The attacker tried to drag him off the tram, kicked him and later threatened him, and is being investigated for a politically motivated hate crime.

Berlin police reported that an unidentified man punched a 60-year-old man to the ground in a park after learning that he was Jewish, and the victim had minor facial injuries. State security police are investigating suspected aggravated assault with an antisemitic motive.
Unknown persons damaged the glass of the synagogue entrance door with stones, and police found a partly burned Israeli flag in front of it, according to the reports. Three suspects were arrested.

About 180 people moved from the station forecourt toward the synagogue in an unregistered rally, and antisemitic chants were shouted, according to a press report. Church bodies described the events near the synagogue as antisemitic riots.

RIAS reports that a resident of an asylum shelter in Coburg attacked another resident with a knife because he took him for a Jew. The Coburg prosecutor's office is reported to have assumed the perpetrator was not criminally responsible.

The entrance door of a residential house in Berlin-Prenzlauer Berg was sprayed with a Star of David. State security police investigated on suspicion of incitement to hatred (Volksverhetzung), and the press reported that the marking apparently aimed to intimidate Jewish residents.
